A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same u-µP research. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite revisions and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original hyperparameter sweeps, transfer experiments, numerical analyses, FP8 training through 7B parameters, and matrix-multiplication benchmarks.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments and reports additional downstream evaluations, sequence-length transfer tests, and initialization-scale diagnostics.

M1.justification: The core parametrization and hyperparameter-search procedure remain unchanged. V2 makes the partial FP8 option already tested in v1 the recommended scheme, keeping critical projections in higher precision instead of using v1's full-FP8 dynamic-rescaling recipe. Section 4.2 specifies approximately 70% FP8 matmul coverage.

E1.justification: V2 adds downstream zero-shot evaluation on MMLU, HellaSwag, OpenBook QA, PIQA, TriviaQA, and WinoGr (Table 4), substantially extending evaluation beyond language-model training losses. WikiText and SlimPajama coverage is retained.

E2.justification: Figure 7 drops the naive FP8 SP and Transformer Engine FP8 SP comparisons reported at 1B in v1. V2 instead compares FP8 u-µP, BF16 u-µP, and BF16 SP at 1B, 3B, and 7B, adding BF16 controls to the larger-scale comparisons.

E3.justification: V2 revises the large-scale precision configuration and replaces the SP baseline's Pythia learning-rate prescription with Llama 3-style inverse-width scaling, using 3e-4 at 7B. It also adds zero-shot evaluation and sequence-length sweeps from 64 to 2048 with either 16K tokens or 64 sequences per batch. The main training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A.5 adds sequence-length sensitivity tests under two batch controls (Figure 11). New Appendix L and Figure 20 diagnose attention, residual, and gradient scale growth at initialization. The earlier 1B full-versus-partial FP8 breakdown is removed from Figure 7, substantially reshaping the supporting analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report three runs per point for the specified learning-rate transfer experiments in Appendix A.5 and 95% confidence intervals in Figure 5. No new repeated-run policy, uncertainty-estimation method, or formal significance test is documented.

E6.justification: Figure 7 replaces the large-scale results under revised precision and baseline settings, rather than establishing same-setting gains over v1. New Table 4 reports MMLU scores of 29.6, 29.0, and 31.2 for SP BF16, u-µP BF16, and u-µP FP8. Figures 11 and 20 add sequence-transfer and initialization-scale findings.

T1.justification: The scaling equations, Lemma F.1 and its proof, hyperparameter derivations, and cut-edge argument are retained. Appendix L adds empirical and mechanistic discussion rather than a new formal result. Section 4.1's notation correction aligns its prose with the embedding learning-rate rule already specified in v1.

C1.justification: The abstract softens 'lower loss' to 'equal to or lower' loss. The FP8 contribution now emphasizes casting most matmuls without dynamic rescaling, consistent with the revised mixed-precision recommendation. The principal parametrization and hyperparameter-transfer contributions remain intact.

C2.justification: New Appendix L attributes depth-dependent scale growth at initialization to correlations induced by causal attention, qualifying the unit-scale assumptions and leaving remedies unresolved. V2 also interprets u-µP's late catch-up to SP as suggesting a different optimization trajectory and discusses precision loss as a possible cause of critical-layer FP8 instability.

D1.justification: V1 promises a future release of the separate large-scale training code; v2 supplies locations for that code and released checkpoints in Section 5.5. Most training tables, hardware information, implementation primitives, and the existing unit-scaling library guide are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds Wang and Aitchison's weight-decay analysis and The Llama 3 Herd of Models. It replaces the GPT-NeoX initialization citation with the already-cited Pythia work. The broader related-work discussion and research positioning remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 consolidates the FP8 explanation in Section 4.2, merges former Sections 5.5–5.7 into Section 5.5, and rewrites the conclusion with a limitations paragraph. These are localized reorganizations; most of the narrative and existing appendices are retained.

P2.justification: V2 replaces Figure 7, adds downstream Table 4 and Figures 11 and 20, revises Figure 3's scaling annotations, and removes the output-distribution row from Figure 6. Figure 1 moves onto the title page. These substantially change the empirical presentation beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens validation of the revised FP8 recipe with BF16 controls at 3B and 7B and downstream evaluations. Appendix L clarifies an important limitation, and reported code/checkpoint access improves reproducibility. These gains are tempered by removal of the Transformer Engine comparison and incomplete editorial integration: Appendix C retains the earlier rescaling guidance, while Appendix J contains a broken reference.
